detailed_sections.section_number_and_title: 3.1 Ancient Foundations: Rock-Cut Caves and Stupas
detailed_sections.full_notes: Early Indian architecture carved entire monolithic temples out of living rock (Ajanta, Ellora Kailash Temple). Stupas like Sanchi served as sacred Buddhist relic mounds enclosed by ornate gateways (Toranas).

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Garbhagṛiha
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: The innermost sacred sanctum housing the main deity in a temple, symbolizing the cosmic center.

detailed_sections.full_notes: Indian builders excels at water conservation structures like stepwells (Baolis / Rani ki Vav) and Vijayanagara aqueducts. Later medieval monuments combined Islamic arches and domes with Hindu stone-carving traditions, giving rise to Indo-Saracenic colonial styles.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Rani ki Vav
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: An exquisite 11th-century subterranean stepwell in Patan, Gujarat, built as an inverted underground temple dedicated to water preservation.

stem_lab_drawers.aim_or_objective: To visually distinguish between Nagara (North Indian) and Dravida (South Indian) temple spires.
materials_or_prerequisites: Reference images of Brihadishvara and Khajuraho temples
procedure_or_steps: Draw a Nagara style temple showing curvilinear beehive spire (Shikhara) topped with an Amalaka.
Draw a Dravida style temple showing stepped pyramidal tower (Vimāna) with a crowned Stupika.
stem_lab_drawers.observations_or_results: Nagara features curved vertical lines; Dravida features tiered horizontal storeys.
stem_lab_drawers.conclusion_or_principle: Regional geography and available stone influenced distinct regional structural styles.
